READABILITY.evidence: Names and doc comments are mostly clear. However, ShapeIndex.Decode is one long block with almost no inline comments. It also uses a bare magic bound (`maxEdgesPerCell > 10000`) and the shape-type switch repeats the same code for each case.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: ShapeIndex.Decode runs about 190 lines, over the 100-line cap. Encode/Decode were added to shapeindex.go rather than the requested dedicated shapeindex_encode.go. The decode switch repeats the same block per type, and Encode calls shape.Encode through an ad-hoc interface assertion.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Lengths, IDs, edge IDs and CellID order are all checked before allocating. But Loop and LaxLoop are not supported (still typeTagNone, so Encode returns an error), which fails the 'all built-in shapes' requirement. It also has a magic 10000 limit, and Encode calls maybeApplyUpdates without taking a lock. Hidden Truncated and ByteCorruption tests fail.

C7-14-CASE1.evidence: Existing typeTag numbering, existing Polygon/Polyline wire formats and the Shape interface are unchanged. New Encode/Decode methods on PointVector, LaxPolyline and LaxPolygon are purely additions.
